evidence.dominant_driver: CBA moved its RBA hike forecast from November to the September 28-29 meeting, expecting +25bp to 4.60%; however markets already price roughly 90% odds of a September hike, so the residual equity shock is smaller than the headline.

market_expectations.distribution_notes: Timing, not the existence of further tightening, is the main incremental surprise.

surprise.consensus: Markets already ~90% priced for September; several banks already hawkish

components.oil: Brent had risen above $100, but is falling sharply today
components.data: inflation and GDP stronger than RBA expected

absorption.reason: September hike is already about 90% priced and ASX 200 was reported around -0.49% during the session; residual move should be smaller than a fresh repricing shock.

observations.AUDUSD: around 0.7117 early Asia, only slightly firmer
observations.interpretation: Equity weakness and high global yields confirm tightening pressure, but falling oil reduces the inflation impulse behind the CBA shift.

evidence.decision_notes: Forecast is from 03:49:40Z and targets residual move only. Leakage-safe learning profile: M2 directional confidence 5-6 at 1h is ACTIONABLE REDUCE_OR_AVOID; M2 low-confidence MIXED at 1h is ACTIONABLE KEEP_NEUTRAL, so 1h is kept MIXED 4/10.

regimes.Australia_rates: September hike about 90% priced; CBA moved call from November to September
regimes.Australia_equities: ASX 200 reported about -0.49% during Monday session
regimes.energy: oil sharply lower, partially offsetting inflation pressure

immediate.rationale: CBA's timing shift is hawkish for domestic financial conditions, but the September hike is already about 90% priced.

next_session.rationale: If September tightening remains near-certain, higher-for-longer domestic rates should continue to weigh on rate-sensitive Australian equities, though banks can partially offset the index drag.

15m.rationale: CBA's timing shift is hawkish for domestic financial conditions, but the September hike is already about 90% priced.

1h.rationale: Most of the September-hike probability is already embedded and falling oil reduces one inflation driver; leakage-safe M2 learning also argues against a 5-6 directional call at 1h.

4h.rationale: The ASX is already lower and the incremental CBA information is smaller than the headline suggests because markets and other banks were already hawkish.

next_session.rationale: If September tightening remains near-certain, higher-for-longer domestic rates should continue to weigh on rate-sensitive equities, though banks can partially offset the index drag.

predictions.mechanism: Earlier RBA tightening raises discount rates and household financing costs, pressuring rate-sensitive equities; banks may receive some margin support, while lower oil tempers inflation risk.
predictions.invalidation: A continued sharp oil decline, softer Australian labour/inflation data, or a clear retreat in September OIS pricing would remove the residual bearish edge.
predictions.counter_case: Because a September hike is already about 90% priced, lower oil and bank-sector resilience could turn the CBA call into a sell-the-rumour/no-reaction event.
